items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 24 at 7:21PM AKST until November 25 at 3:00AM AKST by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
A front continues northward across the panhandle this evening
through tonight, bringing enough moisture into the northern panhandle
and the Haines area to bring another round of snowfall. Snow amounts
3 to 5 inches are expected, the highest amounts past Milepost 24 on
the Haines Highway decreasing down towards the Haines Borough to
around 2 to 4 inches.

* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations of 2 to 5 inches.

* WHERE...Haines Borough, Klukwan, and Haines Border Crossing

* WHEN...Unt
items.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions where available call 511 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 24 at 1:45PM AKST until November 27 at 3:00PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Blowing Snow. Winds gusting as high as 45 mph.

* WHERE...Central and Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM AKST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Areas of blowing snow could significantly reduce
visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...No additional falling snow is expected. Strong
winds will blow snow already on the ground to create areas of low
visibility near the surface. A brief decrease in winds is expected
Wednesday before winds strengthen once more Thursday.
items.areas: Central Beaufort Sea Coast; Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast
items.instruction: Use caution while traveling, especially in open areas.

items.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 24 at 1:23PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
The Department of Environmental Conservation has issued an Air
Quality Alert which is IN EFFECT UNTIL 2 PM AKST THURSDAY.

North Pole has a Stage 2 alert.

Fairbanks has no alert.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 24 at 1:10PM AKST by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
Tidal levels across the panhandle are expected to be running high
for the next few days. These high tides combined with passing low
pressures and their associated fronts could create some
potentially higher than normal water levels. Wind direction,
magnitude, and timing with these systems will be monitored closely as
a combination of high tide and winds in an onshore direction
could lead to tides exceeding astronomical high tide by a foot or
more.
items.areas: City and Borough of Sitka; Western Kupreanof and Kuiu Island; City and Borough of Wrangell; Ketchikan Gateway Borough

items.headline: High Wind Warning issued November 24 at 11:37AM AKST until November 25 at 9:00AM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...South winds 40 to 60 mph with gusts up to 75 mph expected.

* WHERE...Shemya and Attu Islands.

* WHEN...From 1 AM to 9 AM AKST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...High winds may move loose debris, damage property, and
cause power outages. Travel will be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The strongest winds are expected between 5 and
8 AM AKST Wednesday morning, with winds decreasing, but remaining
fairly gusty after 9 AM.
items.instruction:
People are urged to secure loose objects that could be blown around
or damaged by the wind. Prepare for the possibility of widespread
power outages. Use caution if you must drive.
